I'm comfortable across the stack when needed, but I'm happiest owning the data flow: ingest → process → serve → monitor. I containerize services with Docker, work in Agile teams, and use AI-native tooling (Cursor) daily.

items.name: Relay
items.tagline: Enterprise AI operations agent that plans, runs, and validates multi-step business tasks with human approval
items.problem: Companies want an agent that can actually do work across their own tools (databases, documents, Gmail, Calendar, internal APIs) without letting it take unchecked, state-changing actions.
items.solution: Multi-tenant agent platform where companies connect their own tools and a plan-and-execute LangGraph agent completes multi-step tasks, with a human approving every action that changes state.

architecture.description: Next.js frontend, FastAPI API, Celery and Redis workers running a LangGraph plan-and-execute agent, PostgreSQL with pgvector for data, retrieval and memory, plus a pluggable connector layer and isolated code-execution sandbox.
components: LangGraph plan-and-execute agent with capped replanning
Connector registry with manifests, capability model, priority routing and circuit breakers
MCP server and OpenAPI 3 tool import with embedding-based tool search
Code-based approval policy engine with resumable paused runs
Hybrid RAG: pgvector + Postgres full-text search fused via RRF, LLM reranking
architecture.data_flow: Task → plan → capability check → execute step → validate step → replan if needed → approval gate on writes → synthesize answer → groundedness check → user

highlights: Plan-and-execute LangGraph agent with a groundedness check of every answer against step results before it reaches the user
Pluggable connector framework with per-installation circuit breakers so a failing connector fails over to the next one
Any remote MCP server or OpenAPI 3 operation becomes an agent tool with no code changes; embedding-based tool search caps the agent at 20 tools per call
Human-in-the-loop approvals: paused runs survive restarts and resume on any worker, with idempotency keys that prevent duplicate side effects
Hybrid RAG over PDF, DOCX and Markdown with Gemini OCR for scanned PDFs, fusing pgvector and Postgres full-text search via RRF
Security: envelope-encrypted credentials, SSRF guard, read-only SQL guard built on sqlglot, prompt-injection defenses on tool output, per-run budgets
Evaluation harness blocks CI on regressions across routing, text-to-SQL, RAG, planning, groundedness and approval compliance
Design decisions recorded in 15 ADRs

design_system.reference_aesthetic: Restrained technical editorial — think Linear docs meets a personal engineering blog. NOT a SaaS landing page. NOT a Dribbble hero.
design_system.mode: Light preferred — warm off-white background (#F7F6F3 or #FAFAF8), near-black text (#1A1A1A). Single accent: rust/amber (#C45C26 or #B45309). Dark mode optional toggle only — do not default to purple-on-black.

typography.display: Source Serif 4 — weight 600, used sparingly (name + one case study title only)

typography.rules: No Inter. No Space Grotesk. No Cal Sans. No oversized 72px hero headlines. Body 16–18px, line-height 1.6–1.7.

layout.max_width: 720px for prose case studies; 1100px for page shell
layout.grid: Asymmetric — NOT three equal columns. Hero: left-aligned text block, no centered blob.
layout.spacing: Generous vertical rhythm (64–96px between sections). Tight within components.
layout.projects_list: Vertical stack or two-column stagger — each row is name + one-line problem + tech mono line + link. NOT identical glass cards.

design_system.motion: None on hero. Optional 150ms fade-in on scroll for case study sections only. No parallax, no floating elements, no cursor trails.
design_system.imagery: No AI-generated headshots. No stock photos. No gradient orbs. Use typography, whitespace, and optional project screenshot placeholders as bordered rectangles with label 'Screenshot — ForeSyte dashboard'.

Build a personal portfolio website for Inamullah Shaikh — a Computer Science graduate (FAST-NUCES, Islamabad) who builds Python/FastAPI backends, RAG pipelines, and React frontends.

SOURCE OF TRUTH: The Knowledge file JSON. Use ONLY facts from personal, identity, education, experience, projects, and skills sections. Never invent tools listed in not_yet_claimed_on_record. Never fabricate metrics — if metrics_to_add is null, omit that stat entirely.

PURPOSE: A recruiter or engineering manager lands here and within 30 seconds knows: (1) what I build, (2) my two best projects, (3) how to reach me or see GitHub. Secondary goal: deep case studies that survive a technical screen.

USER FLOW:
- Land on / → read one-line positioning → scan ForeSyte + Startup & Law RAG previews → click case study or GitHub
- /projects → filter by category → open case study
- /projects/foresyte and /projects/startup-law-rag → long-form technical write-ups (400–800 words each)
- /about → education timeline + bio from identity.long_bio_paragraphs
- /experience → Komatsu internship
- /contact → email, GitHub, LinkedIn links from personal.contact

PAGES TO BUILD (phase 1 scope — shell + home + routing):
Home, About, Projects index, two case study routes, Experience, Contact. React + React Router. Tailwind CSS.

UI STYLE — READ CAREFULLY, THIS OVERRIDES DEFAULTS:
Editorial engineering aesthetic. Light warm off-white background. Text near-black. Single rust/amber accent for links and focus states only.
Fonts: Source Serif 4 (display, sparingly), IBM Plex Sans (body), IBM Plex Mono (code/stack/dates). Load from Google Fonts.
Layout is LEFT-ALIGNED and asymmetric. No centered gradient hero. No three-card grids. No glassmorphism. No purple. No skill percentage bars. No fake stats. No 'passionate developer' copy.

HOME HERO (exact structure):
- Top: small mono line 'Inamullah Shaikh · Islamabad · CS grad'
- Headline (Source Serif, ~36px): 'I build backends and AI pipelines that have to work in production.'
- Subhead (2 sentences max from identity.short_bio — rewrite in first person, direct tone)
- Row of text links: GitHub · LinkedIn · Email · LeetCode (from personal.contact)
- NO giant CTA button with arrow. Links are enough.

FEATURED WORK (below hero):
Two stacked project blocks (NOT cards in a grid):
1. ForeSyte (Final Year Project) — one sentence problem, one sentence solution, mono tech line, 'Read case study →'
2. Startup & Law RAG — same format

STACK STRIP: single mono line — 'Python · FastAPI · Celery · React · RAG · YOLOv8 · AWS · Docker · SQL'

FOOTER: minimal — © 2026 · GitHub · LinkedIn

TECH: React, TypeScript, Tailwind, React Router. Mobile-first. Lighthouse target 90+. Semantic HTML.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do not add Supabase, auth, contact form backend, or blog unless asked
- Do not use placeholder lorem ipsum — all copy from JSON
- Do not show 'Coming soon' for more than one link total
- Do not add sections not in recommended_pages

# Inamullah Shaikh Portfolio

## Project
Personal engineering portfolio. Source of truth: `docs/portfolio_context.json`.

## Stack
- React 18 + TypeScript + Vite
- Tailwind CSS v4
- React Router v6
- Deploy target: Vercel or Netlify (static)

## Commands
```bash
npm run dev      # local dev
npm run build    # production build
npm run preview  # preview build
```

## Design system (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
Read `docs/portfolio_context.json` → `lovable.design_system` and `lovable.forbidden_vibe_coded_patterns`.

- Light warm off-white `#F7F6F3`, text `#1A1A1A`, accent `#C45C26` only
- Fonts: Source Serif 4, IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono (Google Fonts)
- Left-aligned asymmetric layout — NEVER centered gradient hero
- NO purple, NO glass cards, NO three-column grids, NO skill bars, NO fake metrics

## Content rules
- All copy from `portfolio_context.json` only
- Never invent tools in `identity.not_yet_claimed_on_record`
- ForeSyte is FYP — always listed first in projects
- Omit metrics when null — do not fabricate

## Architecture
```
src/
  components/   # Layout, Nav, ProjectRow, ProseSection
  pages/        # Home, Projects, About, Experience, Contact, case studies
  data/         # portfolio.ts — typed JSON exports
  styles/       # globals, fonts
```

## Workflow
- One page per task unless asked otherwise
- Plan in 5–10 bullets before multi-file changes
- Commit message format: `feat(pages): add foresyte case study`
- Run `npm run build` after each phase — fix TypeScript errors before moving on
